sanskrit: jñānaṃ te 'haṃ savijñānam idaṃ vakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ yaj jñātvā neha bhūyo 'nyaj jñātavyam avaśiṣyate
english: I shall declare to you in full this knowledge together with its realization, knowing which nothing further remains here to be known.

sanskrit: manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu kaś cid yatati siddhaye yatatām api siddhānāṃ kaś cin māṃ vetti tattvataḥ
english: Among thousands of men, scarcely one strives for perfection; and even among those who strive and attain it, scarcely one knows Me in truth.

sanskrit: bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhir eva ca ahaṃkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā
english: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego-sense — thus is My nature divided eightfold.

sanskrit: apareyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām jīvabhūtāṃ mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat
english: This is My lower nature; but know, O mighty-armed one, My other and higher nature, which has become the living soul, by which this world is sustained.

sanskrit: etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇīty upadhāraya ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā
english: Understand that all beings have their womb in these two natures. I am the origin of the whole universe, and likewise its dissolution.

sanskrit: mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyat kiṃ cid asti dhanaṃjaya mayi sarvam idaṃ protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva
english: There is nothing whatever higher than Me, O Dhanaṃjaya. Upon Me all this is strung, like rows of pearls upon a thread.

sanskrit: raso 'ham apsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśisūryayoḥ praṇavaḥ sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu
english: I am the savor in the waters, O son of Kuntī; I am the radiance in the moon and the sun; the sacred syllable Oṃ in all the Vedas, sound in the ether, and manhood in men.

sanskrit: puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaś cāsmi vibhāvasau jīvanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu tapaś cāsmi tapasviṣu
english: I am the pure fragrance in the earth and the brilliance in fire; I am the life in all beings, and the austerity in ascetics.

sanskrit: bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam buddhir buddhimatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham
english: Know Me, O Pārtha, as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent, the splendor of the splendid.

sanskrit: balaṃ balavatāṃ cāhaṃ kāmarāgavivarjitam dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo 'smi bharatarṣabha
english: I am the strength of the strong, freed from desire and passion; and in beings I am desire that is not opposed to dharma, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāś ca ye matta eveti tān viddhi na tv ahaṃ teṣu te mayi
english: And whatever states of being there are — of sattva, of rajas, or of tamas — know that they proceed from Me alone; yet I am not in them, but they are in Me.

sanskrit: tribhir guṇamayair bhāvair ebhiḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat mohitaṃ nābhijānāti mām ebhyaḥ param avyayam
english: Deluded by these three states composed of the guṇas, all this world fails to recognize Me, who am beyond them and imperishable.

sanskrit: daivī hy eṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṃ taranti te
english: For this divine māyā of Mine, composed of the guṇas, is hard to overcome; but those who take refuge in Me alone cross beyond this māyā.

sanskrit: na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ māyayāpahṛtajñānā āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ
english: The evildoers, the deluded, the basest of men do not take refuge in Me; their knowledge carried off by māyā, they cleave to the demonic nature.

sanskrit: caturvidhā bhajante māṃ janāḥ sukṛtino 'rjuna ārto jijñāsur arthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha
english: Four kinds of virtuous men worship Me, O Arjuna: the afflicted, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of gain, and the one who knows, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ jñānī nityayukta ekabhaktir viśiṣyate priyo hi jñānino 'tyartham ahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ
english: Of these, the knower, ever steadfast and devoted to the One, excels; for to the knower I am exceedingly dear, and he is dear to Me.

sanskrit: udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā mām evānuttamāṃ gatim
english: Noble indeed are all of these, but the knower I hold to be My very Self; for, his soul made steadfast, he is established in Me alone as the supreme goal.

sanskrit: bahūnāṃ janmanām ante jñānavān māṃ prapadyate vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ
english: At the end of many births, the man of knowledge takes refuge in Me, realizing, 'Vāsudeva is all.' Such a great soul is very hard to find.

sanskrit: kāmais tais tair hṛtajñānāḥ prapadyante 'nyadevatāḥ taṃ taṃ niyamam āsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā
english: Those whose knowledge is carried off by this or that desire resort to other deities, observing this or that rite, constrained by their own nature.

sanskrit: yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitum icchati tasya tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tām eva vidadhāmy aham
english: Whatever form any devotee desires to worship with faith, that same unwavering faith I bestow upon him.

sanskrit: sa tayā śraddhayā yuktas tasyā rādhanam īhate labhate ca tataḥ kāmān mayaiva vihitān hi tān
english: Endowed with that faith, he seeks to propitiate that form, and from it he obtains his desires — desires ordained by Me alone.

sanskrit: antavat tu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tad bhavaty alpamedhasām devān devayajo yānti madbhaktā yānti mām api
english: But the fruit gained by these men of little understanding is perishable. The worshippers of the gods go to the gods; My devotees come to Me.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ vyaktim āpannaṃ manyante mām abuddhayaḥ paraṃ bhāvam ajānanto mamāvyayam anuttamam
english: The unintelligent think of Me, the unmanifest, as having come into manifestation, not knowing My higher nature, imperishable and supreme.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ mūḍho 'yaṃ nābhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam
english: I am not revealed to all, veiled as I am by My yoga-māyā. This deluded world does not recognize Me, the unborn and imperishable.

sanskrit: vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaś cana
english: I know the beings that are past, that are present, and that are yet to come, O Arjuna; but Me no one knows.

sanskrit: icchādveṣasamutthena dvaṃdvamohena bhārata sarvabhūtāni saṃmohaṃ sarge yānti paraṃtapa
english: By the delusion of the pairs of opposites, sprung from desire and aversion, O Bhārata, all beings fall into bewilderment at their birth, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ tv antagataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām te dvaṃdvamohanirmuktā bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ
english: But those men of virtuous deeds in whom sin has come to an end — they, freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, worship Me, firm in their vows.

sanskrit: jarāmaraṇamokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti ye te brahma tad viduḥ kṛtsnam adhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam
english: Those who take refuge in Me and strive for release from old age and death — they come to know that Brahman in its fullness, the supreme Self, and action in its entirety.

sanskrit: sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ prayāṇakāle 'pi ca māṃ te vidur yuktacetasaḥ
english: Those who know Me together with the Adhibhūta, the Adhidaiva, and the Adhiyajña — they, their minds made steadfast, know Me even at the hour of departure.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kiṃ tad brahma kim adhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktam adhidaivaṃ kim ucyate
english: Arjuna said: What is that Brahman? What is the Adhyātma, the supreme Self? What is action, O best of beings? What is declared to be the Adhibhūta, and what is called the Adhidaiva?

sanskrit: adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko 'tra dehe 'smin madhusūdana prayāṇakāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo 'si niyatātmabhiḥ
english: Who and how is the Adhiyajña here in this body, O slayer of Madhu? And how, at the hour of departure, are You to be known by those of disciplined self?

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasaṃjñitaḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: The imperishable, the supreme, is Brahman; one's own essential nature is called the Adhyātma; and the creative force that brings about the origin of the states of beings is named action (karman).

sanskrit: adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaś cādhidaivatam adhiyajño 'ham evātra dehe dehabhṛtāṃ vara
english: The Adhibhūta is the perishable existence; the Puruṣa is the Adhidaiva; and the Adhiyajña am I Myself, here within this body, O best of the embodied.

sanskrit: antakāle ca mām eva smaran muktvā kalevaram yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: And whoever, at the hour of his end, departs leaving the body while remembering Me alone, attains to My being; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaran bhāvaṃ tyajaty ante kalevaram taṃ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ
english: Whatever state of being one remembers when at the last he gives up the body, to that very state he goes, O son of Kuntī, ever shaped by the thought of it.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yudhya ca mayy arpitamanobuddhir mām evaiṣyasy asaṃśayaḥ
english: Therefore at all times remember Me, and fight. With mind and intellect fixed on Me, you shall surely come to Me alone.

sanskrit: abhyāsayogayuktena cetasā nānyagāminā paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ yāti pārthānucintayan
english: With a mind made steadfast by the yoga of practice, not straying to anything else, meditating upon Him, one attains the supreme, the divine Puruṣa, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: kaviṃ purāṇam anuśāsitāram; aṇor aṇīyāṃsam anusmared yaḥ sarvasya dhātāram acintyarūpam; ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt
english: He who meditates upon the Seer, the ancient, the ruler, subtler than the subtlest, the sustainer of all, whose form is beyond thought, sun-hued, beyond the darkness —

sanskrit: prayāṇakāle manasācalena; bhaktyā yukto yogabalena caiva bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya samyak; sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣam upaiti divyam
english: at the hour of departure, with unwavering mind, endowed with devotion and with the power of yoga, fixing the breath rightly between the brows — he attains that supreme, divine Puruṣa.

sanskrit: yad akṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti; viśanti yad yatayo vītarāgāḥ yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti; tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa pravakṣye
english: That which the knowers of the Veda call the imperishable, which the passion-free ascetics enter, desiring which men practice the discipline of brahmacarya — that state I shall declare to you in brief.

sanskrit: sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca mūrdhny ādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthito yogadhāraṇām
english: Controlling all the gates of the body, confining the mind within the heart, fixing one's own breath in the head, established in the steadfastness of yoga,

sanskrit: om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim
english: uttering the single syllable Oṃ, which is Brahman, and remembering Me — he who thus departs, giving up the body, goes to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ
english: To him whose mind dwells on no other, who remembers Me constantly and without ceasing — to that ever-steadfast yogin, O Pārtha, I am easy to attain.

sanskrit: mām upetya punarjanma duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ
english: Having come to Me, the great souls who have reached the highest perfection do not return to rebirth, that impermanent abode of sorrow.

sanskrit: ā brahmabhuvanāl lokāḥ punarāvartino 'rjuna mām upetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate
english: All the worlds, up to the realm of Brahmā, are subject to return, O Arjuna; but having come to Me, O son of Kuntī, there is no rebirth.

sanskrit: sahasrayugaparyantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ rātriṃ yugasahasrāntāṃ te 'horātravido janāḥ
english: Those who know that a day of Brahmā lasts a thousand ages, and that his night too ends only after a thousand ages — they are the men who know day and night.

sanskrit: avyaktād vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavanty aharāgame rātryāgame pralīyante tatraivāvyaktasaṃjñake
english: At the coming of the day, all manifestations spring forth from the unmanifest; at the coming of the night they dissolve back into that same source called the unmanifest.

sanskrit: bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate rātryāgame 'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavaty aharāgame
english: This same multitude of beings, coming into existence again and again, dissolves helplessly at the coming of the night, O Pārtha, and comes forth again at the coming of the day.

sanskrit: paras tasmāt tu bhāvo 'nyo 'vyakto 'vyaktāt sanātanaḥ yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
english: But higher than that unmanifest is another, an eternal Unmanifest, which, when all beings perish, does not itself perish.

sanskrit: avyakto 'kṣara ity uktas tam āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim yaṃ prāpya na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṃ mama
english: That Unmanifest is called the Imperishable; they declare it the supreme goal, attaining which men do not return. That is My supreme abode.

sanskrit: puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyas tv ananyayā yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idaṃ tatam
english: That supreme Puruṣa, O Pārtha, within whom all beings dwell and by whom all this is pervaded, is to be attained by undivided devotion.

sanskrit: yatra kāle tv anāvṛttim āvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha
english: Now I shall tell you, O bull of the Bhāratas, of the time at which yogins, having departed, go to return no more, and of that at which they go to return again.

sanskrit: agnir jyotir ahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ
english: Fire, light, the day, the bright fortnight, the six months of the sun's northern course — departing then, men who know Brahman go to Brahman.

sanskrit: dhūmo rātris tathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam tatra cāndramasaṃ jyotir yogī prāpya nivartate
english: Smoke, the night, likewise the dark fortnight, the six months of the sun's southern course — departing then, the yogin attains the lunar light and returns.

sanskrit: śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hy ete jagataḥ śāśvate mate ekayā yāty anāvṛttim anyayāvartate punaḥ
english: These two paths of the world, the bright and the dark, are held to be eternal. By the one a man goes never to return; by the other he returns again.

sanskrit: naite sṛtī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaś cana tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna
english: Knowing these two paths, O Pārtha, no yogin is ever deluded. Therefore at all times be steadfast in yoga, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva; dāneṣu yat puṇyaphalaṃ pradiṣṭam atyeti tat sarvam idaṃ viditvā; yogī paraṃ sthānam upaiti cādyam
english: Whatever fruit of merit is laid down for the Vedas, for sacrifices, for austerities, and for gifts — the yogin, knowing all this, transcends it all and attains the supreme, primal abode.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmy anasūyave jñānaṃ vijñānasahitaṃ yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt
english: The Blessed Lord said: To you, who do not cavil, I shall now declare this most secret knowledge together with its realization, knowing which you shall be freed from evil.

sanskrit: rājavidyā rājaguhyaṃ pavitram idam uttamam pratyakṣāvagamaṃ dharmyaṃ susukhaṃ kartum avyayam
english: This is the king of sciences, the king of secrets, the supreme purifier, directly intelligible, in accord with dharma, easy to practice, and imperishable.

sanskrit: aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya paraṃtapa aprāpya māṃ nivartante mṛtyusaṃsāravartmani
english: Men without faith in this dharma, O scorcher of foes, fail to attain Me and return upon the path of death and the round of rebirth.

sanskrit: mayā tatam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagad avyaktamūrtinā matsthāni sarvabhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣv avasthitaḥ
english: By Me, in My unmanifest form, all this universe is pervaded. All beings abide in Me, but I do not abide in them.

sanskrit: na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram bhūtabhṛn na ca bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ
english: And yet the beings do not abide in Me — behold My sovereign yoga! Sustaining all beings, yet not dwelling in them, My Self is the source of beings.

sanskrit: yathākāśasthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni matsthānīty upadhāraya
english: As the mighty wind, ranging everywhere, abides forever in the ether, so understand that all beings abide in Me.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām kalpakṣaye punas tāni kalpādau visṛjāmy aham
english: All beings, O son of Kuntī, return into My nature at the end of a kalpa; at the beginning of the next kalpa I send them forth again.

sanskrit: prakṛtiṃ svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ bhūtagrāmam imaṃ kṛtsnam avaśaṃ prakṛter vaśāt
english: Resting upon My own nature, I send forth again and again this whole multitude of beings, helpless under the sway of that nature.

sanskrit: na ca māṃ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanaṃjaya udāsīnavad āsīnam asaktaṃ teṣu karmasu
english: Nor do these actions bind Me, O Dhanaṃjaya, for I remain seated as one indifferent, unattached to those actions.

sanskrit: mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram hetunānena kaunteya jagad viparivartate
english: Under My oversight, nature brings forth all that moves and does not move; by this cause, O son of Kuntī, the world revolves.

sanskrit: avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanum āśritam paraṃ bhāvam ajānanto mama bhūtamaheśvaram
english: The deluded despise Me, dwelling as I do in a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.

sanskrit: moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ rākṣasīm āsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ
english: Vain in their hopes, vain in their deeds, vain in their knowledge, and bereft of discernment, they cleave to a deluding nature, demonic and fiendish.

sanskrit: mahātmānas tu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtim āśritāḥ bhajanty ananyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam
english: But the great souls, O Pārtha, who have taken refuge in the divine nature, worship Me with minds undistracted, knowing Me as the imperishable source of all beings.

sanskrit: satataṃ kīrtayanto māṃ yatantaś ca dṛḍhavratāḥ namasyantaś ca māṃ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate
english: Ever glorifying Me, striving, firm in their vows, and bowing before Me with devotion, ever steadfast they worship Me.

sanskrit: jñānayajñena cāpy anye yajanto mām upāsate ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham
english: Others too, sacrificing through the sacrifice of knowledge, worship Me — as the One, as the manifold, as variously present, facing in every direction.

sanskrit: ahaṃ kratur ahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhāham aham auṣadham mantro 'ham aham evājyam aham agnir ahaṃ hutam
english: I am the rite, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to the ancestors, I am the healing herb, I am the sacred chant, I am the clarified butter, I am the fire, and I am the oblation.

sanskrit: pitāham asya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ vedyaṃ pavitram oṃkāra ṛk sāma yajur eva ca
english: I am the father of this world, the mother, the sustainer, the grandsire; I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the syllable Oṃ, and the Ṛk, the Sāman, and the Yajus as well.

sanskrit: gatir bhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījam avyayam
english: I am the goal, the upholder, the lord, the witness, the abode, the refuge, the friend; the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the resting-place, and the imperishable seed.

sanskrit: tapāmy aham ahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmy utsṛjāmi ca amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuś ca sad asac cāham arjuna
english: I give heat; I withhold the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and also death; I am being and non-being, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpā; yajñair iṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayante te puṇyam āsādya surendralokam; aśnanti divyān divi devabhogān
english: The knowers of the three Vedas, the soma-drinkers, purified of sin, worshipping Me with sacrifices, pray for passage to heaven; reaching the holy world of Indra, lord of the gods, they enjoy in heaven the divine pleasures of the gods.

sanskrit: te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālaṃ; kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ viśanti evaṃ trayīdharmam anuprapannā; gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhante
english: Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world, when their merit is exhausted they enter the world of mortals. Thus, following the dharma of the three Vedas and craving objects of desire, they obtain only the coming and the going.

sanskrit: ananyāś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmy aham
english: But to those men who, thinking on no other, worship Me — to them, ever steadfast, I bring attainment of what they lack and preservation of what they have.

sanskrit: ye 'py anyadevatā bhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ te 'pi mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhipūrvakam
english: Even those devotees of other gods who sacrifice endowed with faith — they too sacrifice to Me alone, O son of Kuntī, though not according to the prescribed rite.
